reason: The cited evidence shows ML can predict properties of HEAs (E1, E4) and that hierarchical nanoprecipitates strengthen HEAs (E3), but no evidence supports the specific premise that quantitative microstructural descriptors from imaging can be reliably extracted for HfNbTiVAl10 or that adding them to a transformer model yields the claimed error reduction and speed gains. The mechanism premise is partially supported by E3, but the link to fracture behavior and the specific alloy is not evidenced.
premises: Quantitative microstructural descriptors (size, spacing, fraction) can be reliably extracted from high-resolution imaging of HfNbTiVAl10.
Transformer-based ML can correlate multi-scale descriptors with mechanical properties to predict strength and fracture behavior.
Adding microstructural descriptors to thermodynamic features reduces prediction error from ~20% to <10% compared to baseline models.
Hierarchical nanoprecipitates control mechanical response by obstructing dislocations and facilitating load transfer.
ML predictions can be made in seconds, outperforming established simulation methods in speed.
